records.name: Vicenta
records.facts_used: Vicenta: Behind the Name explains Vicenta as the Spanish feminine form of Vincent, which goes back to the Roman name Vincentius and Latin vinco, to conquer. In Klāvs Siliņš’s Latvian dictionary the related form Vicents is placed in the Vincentīna family, but the route by which Vicenta itself reached Latvian use is not described. The name therefore belongs to a well-documented Latin-Christian family, while its local adoption remains less clear. A well-known Spanish bearer is Vicenta María López y Vicuña, born in Navarre in 1847, who in 1876 took the religious habit with two companions, beginning the Religious of Mary Immaculate. Pope Paul VI canonised her on 25 May 1975. This is a Spanish example, not the first use of Vicenta in Latvia.
records.reason: Exact-form bridge and a dated, scoped detail opened in round 56 support two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: INT-BTN curated Vicenta: Spanish feminine of Vincent; Vincent: Vincentius < Latin vinco. LV-SILINS (izpetnieks) Vicenta page: Vicents listed under Vincentīna, no further etymology; its attestation and calendar years are not used because their scope is unclear. INT-VATICAN75 Paul VI homily of 25 May 1975 (canonisation; birth in Navarre 1847, habit 1876, Religiosas de María Inmaculada). Foreign example only; Latvian adoption route unresolved.
